qa.question: Should Bison unit 1 be 759 MW nameplate instead of 745 MW?
qa.finding: The Energy Information Administration table for September 2026 gives 759.0 MW nameplate for the first block, made of a 496.0 MW combustion turbine and a 263.0 MW steam turbine. Basin Electric's release at https://www.basinelectric.com/news-center/news-releases/Basin-Electric-breaks-ground-on-historic-generation-facility says about 745 MW per unit, and the Southwest Power Pool queue entries list 760 MW.
qa.recommendation: Change capacity to 759.0 MW for unit 1 if the team records nameplate, or leave 745.0 MW if the team accepts Basin Electric's net figure.
qa.note: The commission application at https://psc.nd.gov/webdocs/case/25-0086/037-010.pdf gives a net plant figure of about 1,490 MW, which supports 745 MW per block as a net value. I did not open the queue file, so the 760 MW figure comes from the brief.

qa.question: Should Bison unit 2 be 759 MW nameplate instead of 745 MW?

qa.recommendation: Change capacity to 759.0 MW for unit 2 if the team records nameplate, or leave 745.0 MW if the team accepts Basin Electric's net figure.

qa.question: Are the two Sierra Club rows CA1 and CA2 extra Bison units?
qa.finding: No. The Energy Information Administration table at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists CT1 and CA1 as the two turbines of one combined-cycle block and CT2 and CA2 as the two turbines of the second block. The 263 MW rows are the steam turbines, not separate projects.
qa.recommendation: Do nothing. GEM's two combined-cycle units already cover all four generators.
qa.note: A combined-cycle block is one unit in GEM, so the steam turbines are not split out. The Sierra Club data was used only as a lead and is not cited.

qa.question: Does the EIA status of regulatory approvals pending mean Bison is not under construction?
qa.finding: No. Basin Electric reports at https://www.basinelectric.com/News-Center/news-briefs/Construction-continues-at-Basin-Electrics-Bison-Generation-Station that foundation work is under way, and at https://www.basinelectric.com/news-center/news-releases/Basin-Electric-breaks-ground-on-historic-generation-facility that it broke ground on May 11, 2026. The Minot Daily News article at https://www.minotdailynews.com/news/local-news/2026/05/basin-electric-breaks-ground-on-historic-generation-facility/ reports the same event.
qa.recommendation: Keep the status as construction and treat the Energy Information Administration status as out of date.
qa.note: The Department of Environmental Quality issued the air permit on December 29, 2025, according to a saved copy of the Basin Electric news item at https://web.archive.org/web/20260412123005/https://www.basinelectric.com/news-center/news-briefs/Bison-Generation-Station-receives-air-permit.
